safe_directories.description:
Directories to register as git `safe.directory` inside the container.
Injected plugins and the mounted workspace are owned by the host user but
git may run as another user in the container, so without this git refuses
them with "detected dubious ownership". Default: ["*"]; [] disables it.

binary.description: Host path to the binary to inject.

config.description: Host path to a config file or directory to inject.

copy_deps.description: Pack the shared libraries `ldd` finds for the binary (default: true).

target_binary.description:
Where to put an extra wrapper script that runs the binary (default: none:
the binary is on the `PATH` of the sessions lodge opens).

target_config.description: Where the config goes in the container (default: `~/.config/<name>`).

RawAs.description: `"env"`, or a file in the container.

RawFrom.description: Where the value comes from on this machine: exactly one of the three.

shell.description: Shell to launch inside the container (default: /bin/bash).

bundle.description:
A bundle to inject from instead of packing the `[[inject]]` entries: a
file, or a registry as `oci://ghcr.io/me/lodge:1`. A relative file path is
relative to this file's folder.

git.description: Git settings applied in the container.

inject.description: Tools to inject: a binary, a config file or directory, or both.

secret.description: Secrets to deliver at attach time. Local config only, never in a bundle.

session.description: How the interactive session is opened.

target.description: Where to work, unless `--target` says otherwise. Default: docker.

targets.description:
What each target lets you say about it, by target name: `[targets.docker]`.
The keys of a table are checked by the target that reads it.

docker.description: What the user can say about docker, under `[targets.docker]` in the config.

context.description:
The docker context to use (`docker --context NAME`): which engine to talk
to when you have several (a remote one, Colima, Docker Desktop). Default:
the one `docker context use` selected.

docker.title: DockerOptions

kubernetes.description:
What the user can say about Kubernetes, under `[targets.kubernetes]` in the
config.

container.description:
The container of the pod to work in (`kubectl exec -c NAME`). Default: the
one kubectl picks, as for `kubectl exec`.

context.description:
The kubectl context to use (`kubectl --context NAME`): which cluster to
talk to when you have several. Default: the current one.

namespace.description:
The namespace of the pod (`kubectl --namespace NAME`). Default: the
context's.

pod.description:
The pod to work in (`kubectl exec POD`). Every command that uses the
target needs this or `selector`.

selector.description:
A label selector (`kubectl get pods -l SELECTOR`, such as `app=api`) that
finds the pod instead of its name, for pods whose names change. It must
match exactly one running pod: lodge does not pick among several. The pod
is looked up once per run of `ldg`; use it instead of `pod`, not with it.

workdir.description:
The directory in the pod a session starts in. Default: the home of the
user the pod runs as. The project path of `ldg up` is a folder on the host,
so it plays no part here.

kubernetes.title: KubeOptions

podman.description: What the user can say about podman, under `[targets.podman]` in the config.

connection.description:
The podman connection to use (`podman --connection NAME`): which engine to
talk to when you have several (a remote machine, a podman machine).
Default: the one `podman system connection default` selected.

podman.title: PodmanOptions
